Personally, I have serious problems with the weight this entire country puts on biological parenthood. You contribute one fucking cell and we act like it's this lifelong psychic bond. Fuck that. DNA may contribute a lot to the makeup of a child, but I walk around shedding DNA all day long. What matters on a personal, "custody level" is parenting. While you are partly right it's helpful to look into how adopted kids feel. It's so easy to get caught up in the parents and their "rights" but a kid is not a possession it's a developing person that needs nurturing to succeed in the world. As it turns out, having a biological mother and father is by far the best thing for a kid, which is obvious on its face, yet somehow controversial in our modern times. When one of those parents can't do the job we can adjust and do things to make life go better, but it's really doing a disservice to children when we set out from the start to limit their development by not providing the mother and father.

Yes, it's best to have two parents from birth who care and have an interest in the child. But that's not always possible.

I'd be interested to see a study on the well-being of children whose biological parents "reappear" and try to assert custody - my suspicion is that in general this isn't healthy, especially when it's contested.

Have you ever been into building computers? I think it's very much the same. Being a hardware geek is not too dissimilar from being a bike geek. You spend the time learning about and selecting your components based on your budget and your desires/needs and you build a machine that's your own, and you know this when you use it. You will likely also upgrade it over time. The thing you end up with is a beast of your own making. The components you buy are mostly ones you have longed for and eventually attained. There is a freedom there. A pride. A feeling of accomplishment. An achievement of knowledge most people do not share. The performance you get is the one you wanted and made manifest through research and trial, with your hands and your mind. The difference is that with a computer, it's just the performance of the machine that you're tweaking. With a bike is that it's also your body that directly benefits, not just some external thing that performs better and could do so almost without your interaction. The bike is more physically a part of you than a computer, which is more of a mental extension.
